model.rationale: Greg Steube holds a seat with a strong Republican lean, faces a Democratic challenger with minimal fundraising, and markets give him roughly a 95% chance of reelection. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline with a modest nudge toward the incumbent.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or a shift in the national environment toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though an upset would still require a large swing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Republican incumbent Greg Steube is seeking reelection in a southwest Florida district that leans about ten points Republican at the baseline. The political environment this cycle also favors Republicans, adding to the structural advantage he carries as the incumbent. His challenger, Democrat Matthew Montavon, has raised under $100,000 and had only about $24,000 on hand, while Steube has raised $1.3 million and holds more than $2 million in cash. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but has negligible resources.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price Steube at roughly 95 percent. The expected margin sits in the mid-teens for the incumbent, with meaningful but not extreme uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
